coverage_note: Hand-curated for CourtBuilder. Covers 11 franchises across all 5 supported decades (1980s-2020s), not the full NBA. Does NOT claim complete team-season rosters -- only lists the subset of each roster that is also present in the existing 250-player PEAK3 card pool (data/game/profiles/card_profiles.v3.json), AND that pool's model actually resolved a card for (profile_status other than 'excluded' -- v1 listed two players, michael-cooper and jaylen-brown, whose card_profiles.v3.json rows are all profile_status='excluded' at every duration, meaning they were never actually reachable as candidates despite being named; a Phase 5X.5 audit caught this and both were removed here, see per-entry provenance notes). Still deliberately narrow: several combos resolve to only 1-2 eligible candidates (Spurs 1990s, Nuggets at 5yr duration) because no other rostermate from that team/era clears the current all-time-peak-score cutoff into the 250-player pool, or has a resolvable card at every duration. This is a content depth problem, not a bug -- see docs/architecture/PHASE_5X_PLAYER_EXPANSION_STRATEGY.md for why a 250->500 player expansion is required to close these gaps, and why that expansion is about team/era eligibility DEPTH, not about suppressing strong rosters. Not wired into, and not a substitute for, the real team_identity/team_season/team_season_roster_member schema proposed in docs/architecture/PHASE_5_DATA_MODEL.md. Deleted (not migrated) once real team-season data acquisition happens.

team_decade_spins.source_provenance: Public record: Bulls' 1991/1992/1993/1996/1997/1998 championship rosters. Rodman joined in 1995, Ron Harper in 1994, both included under the decade tag (1990s), not claimed for any specific season. Horace Grant was a starter 1987-1994, part of the first three-peat. Note: Ron Harper's card only resolves at the 1yr/2yr durations in the current pool (profile_status=excluded at 3yr/5yr) -- an honest per-duration gap, not an error.

Public record: Lakers 'Showtime' era championship rosters (1980, 1982, 1985, 1987, 1988). Michael Cooper (Defensive Player of the Year, 1987) was part of this roster historically but is deliberately NOT listed here: his card_profiles.v3.json rows are profile_status='excluded' at every duration (insufficient data for a reliable model score), so he is never actually offered as a candidate -- listing him would have been a dead entry, not a real choice.

Public record: Lakers 2000/2001/2002 championship rosters (Kobe Bryant, Shaquille O'Neal); Pau Gasol joined February 2008 and was part of the 2009 championship roster, still within the 2000s decade tag.
Public record: Celtics 1981/1984/1986 championship rosters (Big Three era). Cedric Maxwell was Finals MVP in 1981 and a rotation starter through 1985.
Public record: Celtics 2007-08 championship roster (Garnett/Pierce/Allen 'Big Three'). Rajon Rondo was the starting point guard on that same roster.

Public record: Jayson Tatum, Derrick White (Celtics since 2022), and Al Horford (Celtics since 2021) were all on the 2024 championship roster. Jaylen Brown (2024 Finals MVP, also a real member of this roster) is deliberately NOT listed: his card_profiles.v3.json rows are profile_status='excluded' at every duration, so he is never actually offered -- a v1 dataset bug (see coverage_note) fixed here by swapping in two teammates who do resolve.

Public record: David Robinson's Spurs tenure, 1989-2003; tagged 1990s only for this prototype. No other 1990s Spurs rostermate currently clears the 250-player pool cutoff -- a direct example of the coverage gap documented in PHASE_5X_PLAYER_EXPANSION_STRATEGY.md. Still genuinely 1-candidate after the Phase 5X.5 audit; no in-pool alternative exists.
Public record: Spurs 2003/2005/2007 championship rosters (Duncan, Parker, Ginobili -- the full 'Big Three').
Public record: Warriors 2015/2017/2018 championship rosters (Curry and Thompson throughout; Durant joined July 2016).

Public record: Nikola Jokic (back-to-back MVP 2021/2022, 2023 Finals MVP) and Jamal Murray (Nuggets since 2016, co-star of the 2023 championship run). Jamal Murray's card resolves at 1yr/3yr durations only (profile_status=excluded at 5yr) -- an honest per-duration gap. At 5yr duration this entry is still 1-candidate (Jokic only).

Public record: Bucks 2021 championship roster -- Giannis Antetokounmpo, Jrue Holiday (Bucks 2020-2023), and Brook Lopez (Bucks starting center since 2018). Jrue Holiday's card resolves at 3yr/5yr only, Brook Lopez's only at 1yr -- together they cover this entry at every supported duration, fixing a v1 gap where the 1yr duration had only Giannis.
Public record: Devin Booker (Suns throughout the 2020s), Chris Paul (Suns 2020-2023), Kevin Durant (traded to Suns February 2023).
Public record: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (Thunder since 2019-20) and Chet Holmgren (drafted 2022, debuted 2023-24), core of the Thunder's 2020s rebuild.
Public record: Luka Doncic (Mavericks 2018-2025) and Kyrie Irving (traded to Mavericks February 2023), co-leads of the 2024 Western Conference champion roster.
Public record: Joel Embiid (76ers throughout the 2020s, 2023 MVP) and James Harden (traded to 76ers February 2022).

exact_team_season_spins.source_provenance: Public record: 1990-91 Chicago Bulls roster (first championship team). Dennis Rodman was on the Detroit Pistons this season, not the Bulls -- deliberately excluded here even though he appears in the 1990s decade spin above.

Public record: 1986-87 Los Angeles Lakers championship roster. Michael Cooper (Defensive Player of the Year that same season) is deliberately NOT listed here for the same reason as the lakers-1980s entry above: profile_status='excluded' at every duration, never actually offerable.
Public record: 2015-16 Golden State Warriors (73-9) roster. Kevin Durant did not join the Warriors until July 2016 -- deliberately excluded here even though he appears in the 2010s decade spin above.
Public record: 2022-23 Denver Nuggets championship roster, Jokic's Finals MVP season, with Jamal Murray as his co-star through that exact playoff run. Fixes a v1 gap where this entry was Jokic-only.
